results.summary: This design implements a 256-byte ROM that stores information about the Tiny Tapeout chip, including the shuttle name and commit hash. The ROM is accessed via an 8-bit address on the input pins, and the data is output on the output pins. The first 16 bytes are 7-segment encoded and can be displayed on the on-board 7-segment display by holding reset low and toggling the clock, or by setting the address with DIP switches. The design is intended for educational purposes and to provide chip identification.

This project implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier using full adders and AND gates, as part of the ECE-UY 2204 course. It takes two 4-bit numbers as inputs and produces an 8-bit product. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. It serves as an educational example of digital arithmetic circuits.

This design is a trial implementation of a lightweight all-digital true random number generator based on ring oscillators. It outputs random data via a UART serial interface, and also provides ring oscillator and random generator outputs for observation. Testing requires a UART terminal, a PC for randomness analysis, and an oscilloscope to measure the ring oscillator. The documentation is minimal and the design is experimental.

This design emulates the main peripherals of a Basys 3 FPGA board over a 115200 baud UART link. It handles 16 LED inputs, 16 switch outputs, 12 seven-segment display inputs, and 5 button outputs, communicating via UART RX and TX on the bidirectional PMOD bus. Testing involves using a companion PMOD board or a UART terminal to send and receive the peripheral data. The design is intended for educational or prototyping purposes, allowing interaction with Basys 3 peripherals remotely.

This design implements a multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit for the 16-bit DLFloat data type, intended for deep learning applications. It accepts 16-bit floating-point inputs and produces a 16-bit result, which is output over two clock cycles as two 8-bit halves. An external FPGA is required to drive the inputs and capture the outputs. The design operates at 40 MHz and is notable for supporting a specialized floating-point format.

This design is a dual mixer time differential (DMTD) for audio beamforming using PDM microphones. It accepts PDM inputs from up to eight microphones, along with I2S bit and LR clocks, and outputs PCM audio for each microphone as well as a beamformed PCM output. Delay selection is provided via five pins. The documentation is extremely sparse and does not adequately describe the functionality or testing procedure.

This design implements an approximate multiplier based on the DRUM (Dynamic Range Unbiased Multiplier) architecture, along with a RAM for storing operands and results. It accepts two 8-bit multiplicands and produces an approximate 8-bit product, with results stored in RAM and accessible via an address map. The design requires no external hardware and can be tested by writing operands and reading results. The approximate nature means results may vary with frequency.

This design is a ray tracer that embraces rounding errors as a feature, rendering a 640x480@60Hz VGA output with an animated eye Z coordinate. It was written in HardCaml and includes a test mode that displays color bars. External hardware includes a VGA PMOD and an audio PMOD for sound output. The design is a competition entry for the demoscene and requires a 25.25 MHz clock.

This project is a Verilog-based counter intended to drive a 7-segment display, but the documentation is essentially non-existent. The description states the author has no idea yet, and testing instructions are vague. It requires an external 7-segment display from a demo board. Due to the lack of documentation, the design's functionality cannot be determined.

This is a factory test module designed to verify all I/O pins of the ASIC. It operates in three modes: mirroring input pins to outputs, mirroring bidirectional pins to outputs, or outputting an 8-bit counter on both output and bidirectional pins. The mode is selected by the rst_n and sel pins. Silicon testing confirmed it works as expected.
